rationale: C10 is the strongest plausible template because it is a recent presidential memorandum using the same compact operative machinery: a presidential national-security determination, an express waiver of identified statutory provisions, and a direction to publish the determination in the Federal Register. The child expands that basic formulation with a detailed finding that execution against blocked property would impede foreign policy and sanctions effectiveness. C25 uses essentially the same waiver formula but is earlier and was itself superseded in practical proximity by C10. C08 is substantively related through sanctions waiver and continued blocking of property, but its multi-agency suspension machinery and peace-settlement predicate are less textually aligned.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I hereby determine that the requirements of section 117 ... would impede the ability of the President to conduct foreign policy in the interest of national security ... and, therefore, pursuant to section 117(d), I hereby waive the requirements of section 117 in the interest of national security.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hereby determine and certify that it is important to the national security interests of the United States to waive the provisions of section 1003 of the Anti-Terrorism Act of 1987
shared_material.explanation: Both employ a single presidential national-security finding as the statutory predicate for an express waiver of identified provisions.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Secretary of State is authorized and directed to publish this determination in the Federal Register.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: You are authorized and directed to transmit this determination to the Congress and to publish it in the Federal Register.
shared_material.explanation: The memoranda close with closely parallel directions to the Secretary of State concerning publication, with C10 also requiring congressional transmission.
